steps.content:
<size=40><color=#fb9259>
- Did anyone save the threads discussing Murder on the Praeva Express? I wasn't done reading yet, but then they all vanished when I refreshed. What's going on?

<size=40><color=#fb9259>
- Oh no, the analysis threads I saved are gone too. Someone just said their main account got reported and banned after sharing related content. Pretty sure the mods are doing a purge.

- ****, the invisible hand is making its move! Even the first few chapters of Praeva are gone from the official site now!

- If they're trying so hard to censor this, then it must be real! I've seen something like this before! Is some big shot actually freaking out?
[Background - Eastside Streets. Night]
You put down your terminal and meet up with Nightingale and the arrest squad.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Posts are being mass-deleted online. Whoever's behind this is making their move.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is a rare opportunity, so don't do anything that'll alert the culprit. Contact Doyle and tell him I've obtained new evidence. Let's see if we can get him to investigate from inside the Public Security Bureau one more time.
Eastside elites tend to shield each other. Pull one thread and the whole web unravels. This investigation is going to be tough.

This case falls outside MBCC's jurisdiction. You'll need to quietly pull a few strings if this investigation is to get anywhere. Fortunately, you've been involved in countless incidents over the years, and have built up quite a network across various fields as a result.
Meanwhile, the cordon outside Clementine's residence is lifted.

steps.speaker: Arrest Squad Member
steps.content: Thank goodness nothing went wrong... Surprisingly, she was pretty cooperative this time.
You lead the team toward the car, but pause at the corner to look back at the building.
The corridor lights have already gone dark, the curtains drawn tight. There's no sign of movement. Only the study remains lit.
A vague shadow lingers by the window. You can't tell if someone is standing there, or if it's just the curtain casting a shadow in the light.
You stand there, staring for a while before turning to get into the car.
[Background - Inside the Car]

Nightingale sits in the passenger seat, the glow from her terminal illuminating her face. She briefs you on the personnel arrangements, but when she turns, she notices that your eyes are distant and unfocused. It's clear to her you're not listening.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief? You've been distracted ever since we left. Is something wrong?

options: Sorry, there's just something I still can't figure out.

steps.content: Unease has been gnawing at you since you left. All your questions have been answered, and Clementine has handed over the evidence and leads you needed...
So what are you worried about? What did you miss?
[Flashback: Previous Scene]

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Did you look into it? You couldn't find anything, could you? It's only natural, they're just characters I made up, after all.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Don't worry, I intend to keep our promise. As I said, the book was nothing more than a work of fiction from the very start.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: What I hoped for when I wrote those words... was that perhaps one day, outside the pages of a story, I'd hear someone say them in the real world too.
[Back Inside the Car]

There are more than enough clues, yet they all lead to dead ends when it matters. It's as if someone deliberately dangled them before you, only to pull them away the moment you were about to grasp the truth.
Guided by instinct, you turn to Nightingale with a question.
The other survivors from the Redwood fire... Have we found anything new on them?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: They're proving difficult to track down. The Public Security Bureau's records only cover up to around one year after the fire. There are signs of someone tampering with the archived files, so they've likely been altered too.
You've arrived. You step out of the car and enter a house that can only be described as cramped.
Cough cough... So much dust...
No one's here. Even the windows are boarded up. Clearly, no one's lived here in ages... which is strange. Isn't this supposed to be the sheriff's address?

You scan the room. Only the table by the window stands out. It's suspiciously clean. Barely a trace of dust can be found on it. An envelope sits on the surface. You open it to find nothing but two thin sheets of paper.
...What the?!
N.F. 107 Eastside → Satellite Town Sand Ship Praeva
Passenger List: Williams Park Mary Jones Charles Banbury Allison Pedro
[Scene Transition: Background - Eastside Streets, Night]
A burst of gunfire shatters the still night.

steps.speaker: Arrest Squad Member
steps.content: What was that?!

steps.speaker: Arrest Squad Member
steps.content: Target under attack! Requesting backup, request—

The sound of gunfire doesn't last long. What follows is something far more unsettling—the sounds of a struggle, interspersed with sharp, ominous cracks and snaps. The noise grows louder, mixed with footsteps drawing closer and closer to the villa entrance.

A woman steps out of the villa. Her clothes are spotless, her posture elegant. Her right hand, however, is drenched in blood, all the way from the fingertips to the forearm. At her feet, a mangled figure writhes on the ground, barely recognizable.

steps.speaker: Assassin
steps.content: This power... impossible...

steps.speaker: Assassin
steps.content: How do you... have this much <color=#fb9259>Mania</color>?!

Bang! Another bullet pierces his forehead. The assassin's head lolls to the side, lifeless. The mark on his neck flickers, and it dissolves into a stream of light that flows into Clementine's neck in the next moment.
[Display Clementine's Neck Accessory Portrait, can be layered]
The butterfly taxidermy piece at her neck brims with Mania, greedily absorbing life force. The accessory then converts it into even greater power, feeding it back to its master.

She senses the marks she's planted. One of them is gradually moving farther away. When they parted, she used her ability to leave a mark on ${PlayerName}. It's faint, but it's strong enough to track their location.
A commotion of this scale cannot be hidden, but that's fine. He's clever enough. He should have found the final piece of the puzzle she left behind by now.
steps.female_content: A commotion of this scale cannot be hidden, but that's fine. She's clever enough. She should have found the final piece of the puzzle she left behind by now.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...I'm sorry. It seems I'll have to break my promise.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I said I wouldn't do anything reckless... but alas, we don't live in a fairytale.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I trust you. You will bring change, and those you help will lead fortunate lives... but it's not enough.

Bullets erupt from the barrel, repelling the shadows that lunge at her one by one. Clementine's body is covered in wounds, yet she continues walking steadily toward the exit and into the rain, gun in hand. It's almost as if she's actually unharmed.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Come to think of it, I never told you how that final story ends.
[Black Screen]

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: About Praeva... about the true ending to Redwood's story.
[Scene effect, fire ignites]
Fate is merciful. On the night of the fire, not everyone was trapped inside. The adults and older children were out working odd jobs to make ends meet, so the flames never got to them.
But fate is also merciless. The cheap wooden walls burnt fast—too fast. Those inside could not escape, and those outside could do nothing but watch.
And so... they were separated by the flames. Forever.
[Scene effect, Eastside]

How unfortunate, said the bystanders who witnessed the tragedy. After all, to survive meant despair. To survive meant homelessness and suffering beyond measure. It was better to have perished in the flames and been done with it all.
How fortunate, said the survivors who lived through the fire. After all, to survive meant hope. It meant they still had the chance... the strength to make that bastard pay for what they'd done.
[Scene effect, plotting]
That night, the surviving adults gathered around a single flickering candle, their faces shrouded in shadow, hidden from the light.

steps.speaker: Allison
steps.content: So it was him... Of course. He was the only one who could've gotten inside that night...
They finally found the name. The man was hidden among Redwood's list of sponsors, using his position to suppress any investigation while savoring the victims' suffering from up close.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Jones
steps.content: ...This is our last chance to get close to him. Let's put it to a vote.

No one succumbed to despair. Every heart burnt with an almost zealous fervor. If their voices are too faint, then they will scream until their throats are torn asunder. If their strength is too meager, then they will claw and fight for every scrap. Bloodied and battered, they will use every tool the powerless possess.
Nothing is impossible. Nothing is beyond their reach. Because...
"Justice must be served, and evil must be punished." Even if it means staining their hands.

steps.speaker: Young Clementine
steps.content: Cough, cough... Cough, cough...
Dawn had barely just broken. The adults had packed their bags at some point, seemingly preparing to leave. Clementine dragged her sickly body forward, trying to stop them.

steps.speaker: Young Clementine
steps.content: ...Dean?

steps.speaker: Young Clementine
steps.content: Where... are you going? When will you be back?
No one answered. Their silence spoke for itself. All Clementine received was a gentle hand stroking her head, and a few parting words.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Jones
steps.content: Clementine, you're the one we worry about least... Even when we're not around, you must take care of yourself...

steps.speaker: Mrs. Jones
steps.content: ...Wait here, so you can welcome us home.
Three tickets, three unwavering resolves. They left the child behind and stepped out into the dawn—
Yet they never came back.
[Black Screen + Clementine's Portrait with Downcast Eyes]
The sand ship Praeva vanished 17 hours after departure. All passengers remain missing.
The girl who was left behind searched for a long time. She ventured into the darkness of Eastside, only to find a single ticket and a list.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: <i>An eye for an eye... What a hackneyed approach. They couldn't devise anything more clever or sophisticated, so they decided on a scheme straight out of some old novel.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: <i>But even that didn't work.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: <i>Hope never existed. Justice never smiled upon us. Beautiful fantasy of "an eye for an eye" only happens in novels.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: <i>That's why... I must seek a different kind of power.
[Flashback: Assassination Scene]
In her most desperate times, another hand reached out to her.
I'm sorry, but what you seek is too noble. It is simply something I cannot grant you... No one here is worthy to speak of justice. All I can offer is death.
...But it seems you're not opposed to this power.
Then take it. There's no need to give anything in return. You've already shown me what true love looks like. Now... use this magic wisely.
Your time is running short. I hope you get what you're after.
[Study]

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>... He was an unforeseen variable. At first, she engaged with him only to buy time, waiting for the real prey to take the bait. It should've been over the moment Clementine confirmed that he wasn't a pawn sent by that person.
steps.female_content: <color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>... She was an unforeseen variable. At first, she engaged with her only to buy time, waiting for the real prey to take the bait. It should've been over the moment Clementine confirmed that she wasn't a pawn sent by that person.

steps.content: ...But he was just like the detectives she'd written about countless times. He would rack his brain over every clue, fighting for those who were denied justice, never resting, and never giving up.
steps.female_content: ...But she was just like the detectives she'd written about countless times. She would rack her brain over every clue, fighting for those who were denied justice, never resting, and never giving up.

steps.content: And so, Clementine couldn't help but be drawn to stay by his side, accompanying him through those childish challenges meant only to buy time, guiding him toward the truth.
steps.female_content: And so, Clementine couldn't help but be drawn to stay by her side, accompanying her through those childish challenges meant only to buy time, guiding her toward the truth.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, you were right. Vengeance is nothing more than a naive fantasy that exists only in fiction. It costs far too much. Only a fool would try to seek justice through it.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But... I am a writer, at the end of the day.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Naivety is allowed to exist in stories. Justice is never absent there. Miracles would happen, and whether born of love or hate, all things have a resolution.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Thank you, ${PlayerName}. Thank you for listening to my story, and thank you for showing me... that such a world can still exist.
[Exit Flashback: Back to Reality]
She takes another step forward. The last assassin crumples to the ground.
Mania sears her body. It's not the kind of agony any ordinary person could endure. Clementine's vision blurs, yet her other senses are sharpened to the extreme.

The butterfly ornament finally drains the last of the life force around. It rests at the side of Clementine's neck, now disturbingly lifelike—as though it might tear free from its pin at any moment and take flight.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: And now, it's my turn.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I want to give the people I loved... the ending they should have had.
She steps forward into the rain.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Time to go... The final chapter awaits.
It's long. The surface is clean, dry, with no mud. You run your thumb along the shaft, and your fingers catch on rough wood shavings clinging to the threads near the head.
A man is pacing anxiously, his eyes darting to the terminal screen every so often. On his hand is a ring bearing a prominent family crest.
Vines coil around a set of scales symbolizing justice, seemingly in support. Yet, in truth, they're parasitic in nature. They have woven themselves tightly around it, making it their host.

steps.speaker: Anxious Man
steps.content: Damn it... No matter how many I delete, they just keep coming...
He refreshes the page once more. Still no news of the novelist's arrest.

steps.speaker: Anxious Man
steps.content: What the hell is that useless Minos Chief doing? I should've known one tip-off wouldn't be enough. Good thing I sent my own people too...
Just like countless times before—report, pressure, silence. Even if he makes a mistake, it doesn't matter. The family will shield him.
He thought the last person who knew the truth had gone down with that sand ship. It's been so long now. Why won't she just leave him alone? Why can't she just stay dead?
The phone suddenly rings. It must be the assassin he sent to tail her. He answers immediately, but all he hears on the other end is labored breathing.
A sense of dread suddenly washes over him, but it's already too late.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: At long last... I've found you.
The door suddenly bursts open. The bodyguards are sent flying into the room. Before he can process what's happening, an iron grip closes in around his throat, slamming him to the ground.

steps.speaker: Anxious Man
steps.content: Grk... Argh—
He struggles to speak, but all that comes out are strangled, incoherent sounds.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Do you remember me, Mr. Charles?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Or should I use your old name instead... <color=#fb9259>Carl</color>?
The young children at the orphanage couldn't pronounce Charles properly, so they gave him a nickname that's easier to read—Carl.
And this very same Carl, who was once so kind, personally condemned them to hell.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Once you swap our names, my story becomes the truth.

steps.speaker: Carl
steps.content: Clementine... I'm sorry... please, spare me... I didn't mean to...

steps.speaker: Carl
steps.content: We... we used to get along, didn't we? You'd even bring the children along to tell me stories, remember? I—
Clementine cuts him off.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Shh...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Listen. The clock just struck twelve.

Clementine tosses the gun to the ground, yet the man's expression only grows more terrified. He finds himself unable to move. The strength in his limbs is completely drained, and his eyes are fixated on that eerie, flowing light emanating from the butterfly necklace.
The light grows brighter and brighter, and she begins to speak. Her voice is soft and gentle, almost like she's reading a bedtime story—

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: "The midnight bell chimes. Figures emerge from the darkness, stepping into the chamber. Their eyes unwavering, blades gleaming in their hands."

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: "The first among them tightens her grip on the blade, its tip hovering just above the sinner's heart. She's waiting... waiting for the sinner to open his eyes and see who has come to claim his life."

steps.speaker: Carl
steps.content: It... it was an accident! I didn't want to run, b-but the fire spread too fast, I-I was terrified... You know I've always helped my uncle fund Redwood. I...I would never do this on purpose!

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: "The sinner awakens in agony. He tries to scream, but a second hand clamps over his mouth. A third presses down on his shoulder. It was then that he realized the time had come for him to pay—"
Searing mania spreads across his skin. Under the grip of utter terror, Carl no longer sees Clementine as human. He only sees a monster standing before him.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: "The first stab—this for the innocent souls who perished in the flames."

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: "They withered before they could bloom, trapped in the past before they ever had a future."

steps.speaker: Carl
steps.content: Wait, you want compensation, right? Money? Power? Anything you want, I can give you—
Through his blurring vision, the woman's figure warps and shifts.
The goddess of Justice descends. She weighs his sins upon her scales and brings down her blade to pass judgment.
"The second stab—this is for the souls who perished in WhiteSands before they got their revenge."
"They gave everything to fight injustice, seeking to reclaim justice with their own hands, only to be betrayed once more, buried beneath the sands."

steps.speaker: Carl
steps.content: No... No!
[Transition to Small CG - Assassinating the True Culprit 1]
[Small CG - Assassinating the True Culprit 2]

steps.speaker: Carl
steps.content: —ARGHHHHHHH!!!
Once, twice... The needle falls over and over. The butterfly beats its wings frantically, yet it cannot escape—for it has been pinned firmly to the ground.
"The seventh, and the eighth..."
"The blade falls again and again, blood splattering across the velvet wallpaper of the compartment. The sinner convulses and wails, yet he has still not paid in full."
"The ninth stab cuts through his skin and flesh. The tenth pierces between the ribs. The eleventh... splits open the heart..."
[Small CG - Assassinating the True Culprit 3]
Dark, putrid blood flows without end. The butterfly's struggles grow weaker and weaker, until all twelve needles have fallen. Then, at last, the taxidermy is complete.
"Twelve cuts of vengeance, twelve lives..."
"A blood debt paid in blood."
